body: High. internal/dispatch/stamp.go:94. Split-root synchronization only runs when a frontmatter stamp is newly needed; after sync=failed or sync=halted the stamps are already committed locally, so a retry of dispatch build --stamp skips publication and can emit an envelope against unresolved divergent state. Fix: always run the split-root commit/publish step before worktree creation and envelope assembly, including when stamps already exist.

High. internal/dispatch/stamp.go:85. The status check reads the caller-supplied entityPath, but mutation resolves only its basename under workflowDir. A mismatched path sharing the same slug can validate one entity and mutate another. Fix: resolve the canonical workflow entity path first, require the supplied path to match it after canonicalization, and use that path consistently for validation, mutation, and commit.

High. internal/cli/gate_ceremony.go:42, internal/dispatch/stamp.go:98. Inline workflows receive no commit at any ceremony phase: runGateSync returns immediately for inline state, runStamp commits only split-root state. The updated instructions remove explicit commit steps, so an inline two-command ceremony leaves the Resolution, consumed status, and dispatch stamps uncommitted; a newly created worktree is based on the pre-transition HEAD. Fix: path-scope and commit inline state before routing or creating the worktree, or retain explicit commit steps for inline workflows.

Medium. internal/dispatch/stamp.go:108. Any filesystem object at the expected worktree path is treated as an idempotent worktree, including an ordinary directory or a worktree on the wrong branch. Fix: verify the path is a registered worktree for the main repository on exactly {workerKey}/{slug}; reject other objects and branch identities.

Medium. internal/cli/gate_ceremony.go:85. wrote := result.Consumed || result.ApplicationState == "superseded" mistakes an already-superseded refusal for a mutation (ApplicationState is also seeded on the pure-refusal path per internal/gates/application.go:40). A diagnostic repeat consume in that window can stage/commit/publish unrelated dirty files in the entity's commit unit and can exit 3 (HALT) despite writing nothing -- contradicts the documented byte-clean refusal contract in three places. The new tests cover the consumed repeat-refusal but not this superseded repeat. Fix: add an explicit Wrote/Superseded signal to gates.ConsumeResult set only on successful writes; gate sync on that signal; add a repeat-after-supersede test.

Medium. internal/cli/cli.go:361 vs docs/site/reference/command-reference.md:116. The input.Round != "" record branch writes durable review state but returns before automatic synchronization, contradicting the new reference doc's unconditional "do not re-run state commit after them" claim; the same branch silently ignores --consume. Fix: run runGateSync after successful round publication, or scope the doc sentence to the close/consume forms and state --round still requires state commit; reject --consume with --round as exit-2 usage error.

Medium. internal/cli/gate_consume_sync_test.go:429. TestGateConsumeHaltsOnSameEntityConflict checks cleanliness and remote state but not whether host B retained its divergent commit and consumed application; resetting host B to origin would incorrectly still pass. Fix: assert host B's local HEAD and task.md retain its divergent title and consumed application, and that its branch remains divergent/non-pushable.

Low. internal/dispatch/stamp.go. When an existing worktree= stamp differs from the newly derived path, --stamp still creates the derived worktree though assembly/teardown use the stamped one, leaking an unused worktree+branch. Fix: derive worktree creation from the existing stamped path when present.

Low. internal/dispatch/stamp.go. If the worktree directory is gone but {worker_key}/{slug} still exists, git worktree add -b fails because the branch already exists. Fix: detect the existing branch and use git worktree add <path> <branch>.

Low. Gate synchronization path using syncActiveEntity. Unlike runStateCommit, the gate path can create a commit before discovering a wrong branch or an in-progress rebase during publication preflight. Fix: run statesync.Preflight before staging or committing.

Low. fo-dispatch-core.md. The final landing-table row says advanced and terminal outcomes end with a sync= line, while terminal unspent routes emit no sync line. Fix: split terminal routing into a separate row and describe branching on route=.

Low. runStateCommit and syncActiveEntity error formatting. Errors can become "git commit failed: git commit failed: ..."; not-found and archived-scope errors are also mislabeled as commit failures. Fix: preserve the underlying error category and avoid duplicate prefixes.

Low. stampFixture and TestSharedCoreRemainsBelowPreChangeByteCap. worktreeStage parameter is unused; the fixture comment names the wrong state path; the historical byte-cap test now numerically duplicates the current component-cap assertion. Fix: remove or use the parameter, correct the comment, and either restore the historical invariant or remove the duplicate test.

reason: Synthesis verdict F: changes should not merge yet -- three high-severity synchronization and path-integrity defects can dispatch workers from stale or incorrect state.

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: no shipped workflow declares a per-stage agent override today, so the derived and stamped worktree paths never actually diverge in production; promotes-when: a shipped workflow adds a stage-level agent override after an entity's worktree was already stamped under a different worker key

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: the stamp worktree-add path only runs when the path is absent, and the supported recovery flow, state commit then rerun, never leaves the branch behind without the directory; promotes-when: an operator manually removes the worktree directory through a path outside the documented recovery procedure while leaving the branch intact

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: the ordering only surfaces on a checkout already in an unsupported state, a wrong branch checked out or a rebase left in progress, which the existing HALT and refusal contract already treats as an operator-intervention case; promotes-when: a supported concurrent-writer scenario reaches this ordering before the checkout is known-good, producing a commit that Preflight would otherwise have refused

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: this is a documentation clarity gap in the landing-position table parenthetical, not a behavioral defect, since the code's actual sync-only-when-wrote rule is unambiguous and covered by TestGateConsumeOnTerminalRouteEmitsNoSyncLine; promotes-when: an FO or ensign misreads the table and manually invokes a sync after a terminal route based on the ambiguous row

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: the doubled prefix and mislabeled categories are stderr wording only, the exit code and machine-parseable sync=/phase= line remain correct, so no caller branches on the prose; promotes-when: a caller starts pattern-matching this stderr text for error classification instead of the exit code and the sync=/phase= line

class: correct-but-disproportionate; why-not-material: the unused parameter, the stale comment, and the duplicated cap assertion are test-corpus readability only, both cap tests already pass at the correct raised ceiling; promotes-when: a future change relies on stampFixture's worktreeStage parameter actually varying behavior, or the two cap tests are allowed to drift to different values
